question: Metal-on-metal (MoM) hip resurfacing and large-head total hip arthroplasty were withdrawn or restricted primarily because of a higher rate of dislocation compared to conventional metal-on-polyethylene bearings.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. MoM implants were withdrawn due to ARMD — adverse reaction to metal debris (cobalt-chromium ion release → pseudotumours, metallosis, soft-tissue destruction, systemic cobaltism). Paradoxically, larger femoral heads reduce dislocation risk. The MoM cautionary tale is the most important lesson from recent arthroplasty advances.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. MoM implants were not primarily withdrawn because of dislocation risk. They were withdrawn or restricted because of ARMD (adverse reaction to metal debris): cobalt-chromium ion release caused pseudotumours, metallosis, soft-tissue necrosis, and systemic cobaltism. Dislocation risk was actually lower with large-head MoM designs due to the increased head size.
